intro: A bowl of restaurant ramen has an estimated 650 kcal. Most of the calories come from the ramen noodles and the rich, fatty broth.
diet: Yes, especially when you're eating out with family or friends. Rich broths like paitan or tonkotsu are high in fat. Choose a clear broth and don't finish the soup, this makes a big difference. Balance it with a lighter breakfast and dinner.
tips: Choose clear broth like shoyu or shio.
Leave at least half the broth.
Skip side orders like fried gyoza or rice.

swap.name: Clear broth ramen + egg, without drinking the broth
swap.why: Less fat from the broth, and you still get protein from the egg and meat.

faq.a: Original tonkotsu uses pork bones. Many halal restaurants now use chicken or beef broth. Check the shop's halal certificate.

faq.q: What's the difference between tonkotsu, shoyu and miso ramen?
faq.a: Tonkotsu is a thick white broth from bones. Shoyu is soy sauce-based and clearer. Miso uses soybean paste and tastes richer.

faq.q: Is instant ramen the same as restaurant ramen?
faq.a: No. Restaurant ramen uses fresh noodles and broth simmered for hours. Instant noodles are usually fried and high in salt.
